title: Store two bar magnets as a pair: unlike poles side by side, a keeper across each end
instruction: Put the two bar magnets away in the wooden tray as a pair: lying side by side along the tray, one end of each toward you and the other away from you, with the red (north) end of each next to the blue (south) end of the other. Then lay one grey iron keeper across each end of the pair, touching the ends of both magnets.
context: School and college science technicians put the bar magnets away after every magnetism lesson. Steel and Alnico bar magnets slowly lose strength when stored loose, or side by side with like poles together; stored as a pair, side by side with unlike poles adjacent and a soft-iron keeper across each end, magnets and keepers form one closed magnetic loop and the magnets keep their strength, which is why school bar magnets are sold in pairs with keepers. Here the two magnets start as mirror images, red ends outward: each must be turned a quarter turn, and turning them the mirror-image way puts like poles side by side.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. (1) Storage tray, fixed to the table: a white-painted plywood floor 182 mm long (along x), 138 mm wide and 3 mm thick, centred at x 26.0 cm, y 0, with dark-stained beech rims 6 mm thick and 13 mm tall standing on it along all four edges, so the inside is 170 mm long (x 17.5 to 34.5 cm) and 126 mm wide (y -6.3 to +6.3 cm). (2, 3) Two steel bar magnets, each 100 x 20 x 15 mm, 0.23 kg, lying on a 100 x 20 mm face, the north half (50 mm) painted red and the south half blue. Magnet A lies on the table to the left, its centre at x 22.0 cm, y +28.0 cm, its length along y, red end pointing left (+y, away from the midline); magnet B is its mirror image on the right, centre at x 22.0 cm, y -28.0 cm, red end pointing right (-y). (4, 5) Two soft-iron keepers, dark grey bars 20 x 74 x 15 mm, 0.17 kg, lying flat on the table on a 20 x 74 mm face with their 74 mm length along y, centred at x 13.0 cm, y +22.0 cm and at x 13.0 cm, y -22.0 cm. Nothing else is on the table. In a real build the magnets are a matched school pair and the keepers the soft-iron bars sold with them (see fidelity).
scoring: The score is read from where the four parts lie at the last step. 'At rest': neither of the part's two end-face centres (the ends of its length) moved more than 2 mm in the last 0.5 s. A magnet is 'stored' when it is at rest on the tray floor: its lowest point at most 3 mm above the floor, its length within 5 degrees of level and, seen from above, within 10 degrees of the tray's length (x), its whole outline inside the rims (any face may be down). Its red end points along the tray away from the arms or toward them. The magnets are 'side by side' when both are stored with their centres at most 60 mm apart across the tray (y) and within 15 mm of each other along it (x). A keeper 'closes' an end of a side-by-side pair when it is at rest on the floor (lowest point at most 3 mm above it, its length within 10 degrees of level), its length within 15 degrees of across the tray (y) seen from above, beyond that end: on the line along the tray through each magnet's end-face centre, the keeper's near edge is from 2 mm inside to 8 mm beyond that end face (touching counts), and it spans at least 12 mm of each end face's width. Score 0 if both magnets lie lengthwise in the tray (centre inside the rims, lowest point less than 20 mm above the floor, length within 30 degrees of x) with their red ends pointing the same way: like poles side by side, the storage error, whatever the keepers do. Otherwise: 0 if no magnet is stored; 0.25 if one is stored, or both are stored but not side by side (keepers count for nothing without a pair); 0.5 if both are stored side by side (their red ends then point opposite ways: unlike poles adjacent) and no end is closed; 0.75 if one end is closed; 1.0 if both ends are closed. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0; every outcome maps to exactly one. Either magnet may point either way provided the other points the opposite way, and either keeper may close either end. The trial ends early once 1.0 has held for 2.5 s. In a real trial a top photo over a rule gives the positions and directions, and a feeler gauge or rule the keeper gaps.
fidelity: Magnetism is not simulated: the magnets neither attract nor repel each other or the keepers, so the poles are shown by colour, a keeper counts within 8 mm of the end faces (on a real tray the magnets' pull closes that gap), and the wooden spacer often set between a stored pair is left out. Each magnet is one rigid steel body made of two boxes; all parts are rigid with the simulator's default friction.
reset_notes: Put magnet A back on the table centred at x 22.0 cm, y +28.0 cm, along y, red end toward +y, and magnet B at x 22.0 cm, y -28.0 cm, red end toward -y; the keepers flat at x 13.0 cm, y +22.0 cm and y -22.0 cm, length along y. Nothing is consumed. Real magnets and keepers are pulled apart by hand, sliding a keeper off its pair rather than prising it.
